phases.name: Harness and agent-contract remediation
phases.goal_note: None. Phase 26 is internal harness maintenance: it changes no product behavior, no product code, and no v1.3 artifact identity. It is deliberately outside the goal/DG/ADR machinery - no `G` number, no `DG` number, and no new ADR. A phase reviewer must not read the absent goal or decision gate as a missing-goal defect.
phases.objective: Put the agent harness and its contract in the state v1.3's own product phases and build/live/security/release cycle require: an amended phase-21 orchestration record, enforced corrective and evidence-integrity rules, machine-enforced guards for the two record-keeping classes that recurred in v1.2, corrected agent prompts, a working session-usage collector, and an advisory re-review showing which previously advisory classes the new guards now cover.
deliverables: A purely additive amendment to docs/implementation/phase-21/orchestration.json: the contract-required `subagents` array and a conforming `aggregate` recomputed from the task-level records, with the amendment recorded in that record's own `notes`.

Agent-contract rules A1-A7 in docs/agent-contracts.md: corrective/re-derivation, invocation and evidence integrity, the tightened reports-array rule, the phase-gate security-disposition obligation, the enforcement-scope entries, the release-phase gate precedent, and the conditional doc-budget raise.

Guard enforcement in scripts/check-agents.sh: from phase 20 a task's state.json `reports` array lists every on-disk preserved `.attempt-<n>.json`; from phase 26 a phase-level orchestration record carries `subagents` and an `aggregate` whose numeric fields equal the sums recomputed from the task records, plus the matching scope constant and its self-check.

The seven prompt corrections in .opencode/agents (orchestrator, implementation-reviewer, implementation-planner, live-host-verifier, test-quality-reviewer, security-reviewer, phase-reviewer/release-reviewer).
A session-usage collector that reads the resolved server's /api/session/<id> directly instead of through `opencode api get`, keeping the never-estimate contract.
An advisory agent-process re-review recording whether the new guards cover the previously advisory classes.
A recorded sensitivity probe per new guard: each guard fails on a deliberately broken input and passes when the input is restored.

tasks.name: Agent-contract rules
tasks.traceability: Process remediation of the v1.2 release-review and phase-20 agent_process observations. Not tied to a goal or ADR.
work: A1 corrective/re-derivation rule: after any artifact re-derivation, sweep superseded identities (docs/testing/, docs/release/, the changelog, ADR implementation notes) and mark each occurrence superseded; and do not start a full artifact/live/security re-derivation while a corrective set is open without a consolidated adversarial pass over the fix batch or explicit user sign-off.

A2 invocation/evidence-integrity rule: retry an attempt-0 invocation whose report is absent before treating it as an outcome; run destructive pre-fix probes in an isolated export or worktree rather than the shared tree; treat a no-build result as valid only after a rebuild when another agent may have touched the tree; and check a causal procedure claim against the pinned research before recording it.
A3 tighten the reports-array rule to require every preserved `.attempt-<n>.json` on disk for each listed report.

A4 a phase-gate obligation to record an explicit per-finding security disposition (fix-now / accept-with-register-entry / defer-with-rationale, the user owning an accept) before the next phase starts.
A5 the enforcement-scope entries for A3 and for the 26.3 aggregate guard, agreeing with the scope constants in scripts/check-agents.sh.
A6 the release-phase gate precedent: following the v1.1 Phase 14 precedent, the release review is the release-phase gate and no separate phase-reviewer record is produced.
A7 raise the docs/agent-contracts.md budget line in scripts/check-docs.sh only if an enforced rule actually requires it.
tasks.tests: `bash scripts/check-docs.sh` budget passes; the enforcement-scope numbers stated in the contract agree with the constants in scripts/check-agents.sh (the existing self-check is the enforcement); a diff review confirms each of A1-A7 is present and stated once.
acceptance_criteria: Rules A1-A7 are present in docs/agent-contracts.md.
tasks.documentation: docs/agent-contracts.md; scripts/check-docs.sh (budget line only, and only if required)
